seo_title: Maybank Case Study: Singapore Bank Content | SOMIN
description: SOMIN compared Maybank, CIMB, Citi, HSBC and UOB content in Singapore, mapping 5 audience segments, 6 pain points and the moments money worries peak.
h1: Maybank and 4 rivals lead with community, but money fears stall decisions
lede: SOMIN read Instagram, Facebook and ad library content from Maybank, CIMB, Citi, HSBC and UOB published between 2022 and 2024. Community Support was the most identified interest, found 1,815 times, and the content clustered into 5 audience segments and 6 pain points. SOMIN then planned broad and micro moments and built story-based insights for one segment.
meta_line: A SOMIN brand briefing · 2022 to 2024 · Singapore

challenge.title: Maybank against CIMB, Citi, HSBC and UOB on posts and ads
challenge.body: Maybank competes for attention with CIMB, Citi, HSBC and UOB across social posts and ads. The study looked at who these banks talk to, which pain points they address and which moments a brand could use. Data from 2022 to 2024 was sparse, with a collection cap applied.

approach.title: From 10 top interests to personas, moments and stories
points: Collected Instagram, Facebook and ad library content for 5 banks, from 2022 to 2024.
Ranked the top 10 interests, led by Community Support (1,815), Savings (1,570) and Travel (1,240).
Segmented the audience into 5 personas and the messaging into 6 pain points, by post count and engagement.
Picked one pain point and planned broad and micro moments, each with an addressable tension.
Paired one segment with that pain point and its sociological and psychological reasons to write story-based insights.

findings_title: Community interest, ad-heavy rivals and personal-finance fears

findings.title: Community tops the interest list
findings.body: Community Support was identified 1,815 times, ahead of Savings (1,570), Travel (1,240) and Loyalty Programs (1,147). Finance came fifth at 827.

findings.title: UOB and HSBC lean on ads
findings.body: UOB had the biggest footprint with 593 posts and 955 ads. HSBC ran 757 ads against 88 posts, while Maybank published 520 posts and 244 ads.

findings.title: Personal finance is the pressure point
findings.body: The Navigating Personal Finance Challenge pain point covers money management, low financial literacy and economic uncertainty. SOMIN linked it to fear of financial insecurity and the desire for instant gratification.

delivered.title: Maybank's 5 segments, 6 pain points and moment plans
points: 5 audience segments, from Financial Stability Seeker to Community-Minded Advocate for Connection and Belonging
6 pain points, including financial scams and vulnerabilities in banking, and travel risks and financial concerns
Broad moments such as festive season financial preparedness, and micro moments such as checking bank balances at the end of the month
Sociological and psychological reasons behind the tension, each tied to an applied theory
An imagined character and two sample stories built on one segment and one pain point

quote.text: Fear is a shackle; knowledge is the key

outcome.title: Maybank can answer fear of financial insecurity with knowledge
outcome.body: The study shows how one pain point becomes a usable story: fear of financial insecurity, answered with understanding and connection. Micro moments such as an end-of-month balance check, a pay rise or an unexpected bill give Maybank specific times to say it.

faq.q: Which banks were in the Maybank study?
faq.a: Maybank, CIMB, Citi, HSBC and UOB. SOMIN collected their Instagram and Facebook posts and ad library content from 2022 to 2024.

faq.q: What is the difference between broad and micro moments?
faq.a: Broad moments are wider occasions, such as festive seasons or property fairs. Micro moments are specific instants, such as seeing late fees on a credit card bill, each paired with an addressable tension and the consumer's thought.

faq.q: Is the character in the stories a real customer?
faq.a: No. SOMIN imagines a character that embodies an audience segment, then combines it with a pain point and a psychological reason to write a story-based insight.
